exam.title: ASMOPSS X — Science Primary (Theoretical Round)
exam.subject: science
exam.instructions: Đề gồm 3 phần, 40 câu, 100 điểm. Phần 1: 20 câu trắc nghiệm, 1 điểm mỗi câu — chọn một phương án (A–E). Phần 2: 10 câu trả lời ngắn, 2 điểm mỗi câu — gõ đáp án; câu có nhiều chỗ trống được đánh số (1), (2), … và chấm điểm theo từng chỗ trống. Phần 3: 10 câu tự luận, 6 điểm mỗi câu — trình bày lập luận; riêng câu yêu cầu vẽ hình thì chụp ảnh hình vẽ rồi tải lên. Không dùng máy tính. Hình vẽ không theo tỉ lệ.

_notes.source: Final ASMOPSS X/ASMOPSS X, Science Primary.pdf + ASMOPSS X, Answer Key Science Primary.pdf
_notes.numbering: Đề gốc đánh số lại từ 1 ở mỗi phần. Ở đây dùng số toàn cục 1–40 GIỐNG file đáp án: Part 1 = 1–20, Part 2 = 21–30 (đề in là 1–10), Part 3 = 31–40 (đề in là 1–10).
_notes.scoring: Part 1: 20×1 = 20. Part 2: 10×2 = 20. Part 3: 10×6 = 60. Tổng 100, đúng như đề in.
_notes.grading_choice: Part 2 và Part 3 để grading_mode='essay' kèm barem chứ không dùng 'exact', vì barem gốc chấm theo từng ý (0,5–2 điểm mỗi ý) trong khi 'exact' chỉ so đúng một chuỗi và được ăn cả ngã về không. Hệ quả: 20 câu này cần khóa AI mới chấm được; 20 câu Part 1 vẫn chấm máy tức thì và miễn phí.
_notes.images: Hình được RENDER thẳng từ vùng trang PDF (không bóc ảnh nhúng) để giữ cả hình vector lẫn nhãn A./B. cạnh hình. Câu 3, 5, 6, 10 có phương án LÀ HÌNH nên options chỉ ghi A–E, phải nhìn hình mới chọn được.
flags: Câu 19 (cầu vồng): đáp án chính thức là B (bán kính cung tăng). Chiết suất lớn hơn làm góc cầu vồng NHỎ đi, tức bán kính giảm — theo đó phải là C. Đã giữ nguyên đáp án chính thức; cân nhắc đối chiếu trước khi dùng chấm điểm thật.

questions.prompt_md:
Study the following organisms.

Which characteristic(s) do all three animals have in common?

1. lay eggs
2. have lungs
3. have scaly skin
4. give birth to their young alive
options: 1 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
3 and 4 only

questions.prompt_md: Liver cells of a male Indian elephant have 56 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in its sperm?
questions.solution_md: Sperm are gametes, produced by meiosis, so they carry half the diploid number: $56 \div 2 = 28$.

questions.prompt_md:
Linda conducted an experiment on photosynthesis in a dark room using the set-up shown below. She measured the amount of gas collected in the measuring cylinder after some time.

The graphs below show the amount of gas collected plotted against different variables. **Which of the following graphs shows the correct amount of gas collected?** (Choose the letter of the graph.)
options: A
B
C
D
E
questions.solution_md: The lamp is the only light source in a dark room, so light intensity — and therefore the rate of photosynthesis and the amount of oxygen collected — falls as the lamp is moved away. The correct graph plots the gas collected **decreasing** with the distance between the lamp and the water plant.

questions.prompt_md:
A student conducted a food test experiment. A food sample made iodine solution colorless.

What substance is in the food sample?
options: Starch
Glucose
Vitamin C
Protein
Fat
questions.solution_md: Starch would turn iodine blue-black. Decolorising the iodine instead is the classic test for **vitamin C** (ascorbic acid), which reduces iodine to colourless iodide.

questions.prompt_md:
A plastic rod with a positive charge is held near a neutral sphere suspended by an insulating thread. Then the sphere moves closer to the plastic rod.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The sphere becomes positively charged and the tension on the thread increases.
The sphere becomes negatively charged and the tension on the thread decreases.
The sphere becomes polarized and the tension on the thread is unchanged.
The sphere becomes polarized and the tension on the thread increases.
The sphere becomes negatively charged and the tension on the thread increases.
questions.solution_md: The sphere stays neutral overall — the rod merely **polarizes** it, pulling negative charge to the near side. The resulting attraction has a horizontal component, so the thread hangs at an angle and its tension increases.

questions.prompt_md:
A toy boat is placed on the surface of the water in a container.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: If initially the container is full of water, the water pressure at the bottom of the container will increase.
If initially the container is full of water, the water pressure at the bottom of the container will decrease.
If initially the container is only half full, the water pressure at the bottom of the container will increase.
Whether the container is full or not, the water pressure at the bottom of the container will increase.
Whether the container is full or not, the water pressure at the bottom of the container will stay the same.
questions.solution_md: The floating boat displaces its own weight of water, so the water level rises and the pressure at the bottom goes up — but only if there is room for the level to rise. In a container that was already full, the displaced water simply spills over and the depth is unchanged.

questions.prompt_md:
As a warm liquid cools, its temperature is measured. The graph below shows how the temperature changes as a function of time.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: After 2 minutes all liquid becomes vapor.
The boiling point of the liquid is 65 °C.
From 2 minutes to 5 minutes no heat is transferred out.
From 2 minutes to 5 minutes some liquid becomes solid.
From 2 minutes to 5 minutes some liquid becomes vapor.
questions.solution_md: The flat section of a **cooling** curve is a change of state at constant temperature. Since the substance is cooling, that plateau is freezing: some of the liquid is turning into solid while heat continues to leave.

questions.prompt_md:
A smartphone with a battery capacity of 3000 mAh is connected to a power supply, and goes from zero to fully charged in 60 minutes.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Electric charges in the battery increase by 10800 C.
Electric charges in the battery decrease by 10800 C.
Electric charges in the battery increase by 1800 C.
Electric charges in the battery decrease by 1800 C.
Total electric charges in the battery don't change.
questions.solution_md:
The trap is to compute $3000\text{ mAh} = 3\text{ A} \times 3600\text{ s} = 10800$ C and pick that. But that is the charge pushed *through* the circuit, not the battery's own net charge.

A battery stays electrically **neutral**: for every electron that enters one terminal, one leaves the other. Charging stores chemical energy and rearranges charge internally — the total electric charge in the battery does not change.

questions.prompt_md:
Alex lights a candle placed behind a converging lens, outside the lens focal length. After looking carefully in front of the lens, Alex couldn't see the image.

What should he do to see an inverted image?
options: Step back farther from the lens.
Place the candle at the lens focal point.
Place the candle closer to the lens.
Replace the lens with one of longer focal length.
Use a bigger candle.
questions.solution_md: With the object outside the focal length a **real, inverted** image is already formed in front of the lens. Alex sees nothing because his eye is at or inside that image. Stepping back puts the image in front of his eye, where he can focus on it.

questions.prompt_md:
A fish stays at rest underwater.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The force by the water from below the fish equals the force of gravity on the fish.
The force by the water from below the fish equals the force by the water from above the fish.
The force by the water from below the fish must be stronger than the force by the water from above the fish.
The force by the water from below the fish must be weaker than the force by the water from above the fish.
The force of gravity on the fish must be stronger than the force by the water from above the fish.
questions.solution_md: Water pressure increases with depth, so the upward push on the underside exceeds the downward push on top. That difference **is** the buoyant force, and it is what balances the fish's weight.

questions.prompt_md:
A warship sends pulses of sound to detect a submarine. It sends the pulses every second. After 3 seconds it receives back the first pulse, and the next pulse after that with a little bit more than a one-second interval.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The submarine moves closer to the warship.
The submarine moves farther from the warship.
It takes 3 seconds for the first pulse to reach the submarine.
It takes 2 seconds for the first pulse to reach the submarine.
It takes 4 seconds for the first pulse to reach the submarine.
questions.solution_md: Echoes arriving **more** than one second apart mean each successive pulse has a longer round trip than the one before, so the submarine is moving away. (The 3 seconds is the round trip, so the outward leg takes 1.5 s, not 3 s or 2 s.)

questions.prompt_md:
Two different spheres are made of different materials, initially at the same temperature of 80 °C. Sphere A reaches room temperature faster than sphere B.

Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The radiated power of sphere A must be higher than sphere B.
Total heat flowing out from sphere A must be higher than sphere B.
Heat conductivity of sphere A must be higher than sphere B.
The heat capacity of sphere A must be higher than sphere B.
None of the above statements are correct.
questions.solution_md: Cooling faster only tells us the ratio of heat loss to heat capacity is larger for A. Any single one of the listed quantities could go either way — for instance A could simply have a much smaller heat capacity — so none of the statements must be true.

questions.prompt_md: A rainbow appears because of refraction, dispersion and internal reflection of sunlight by droplets of water in the air. If the droplets of water are replaced by droplets of a different liquid with a higher index of refraction, what will happen?
options: Nothing changes.
The arc radius of the rainbow increases.
The arc radius of the rainbow decreases.
Blue color disappears from the rainbow.
Red color disappears from the rainbow.

questions.prompt_md:
A pendulum is pulled to the left then released. After 41 seconds, the pendulum has passed through the middle of its swing 21 times.

What is the period of the pendulum's oscillation?
questions.solution_md:
Released from one extreme, the bob first crosses the middle after a quarter of a period, then once every half period after that. The 21st crossing happens at

$$\frac{T}{4} + 20 \times \frac{T}{2} = 10.25\,T = 41\text{ s} \Rightarrow T = 4.0\text{ s}.$$

**State two organs that produce substances to neutralize chyme.**

questions.prompt_md:
Theodore Engelmann conducted an experiment to prove which colors of light (wavelengths) are effective for photosynthesis. He illuminated a strand of filamentous algae with different colors of light. He added aerobic bacteria to this set-up and noted where the bacteria accumulated. The picture below shows the result of the experiment.

**a.** The aerobic bacteria need oxygen to survive. State 2 other characteristics of living things shown by the aerobic bacteria during the experiment.

**b.** State the conclusion of the experiment.

rubric.description: a) First characteristic: movement — the bacteria move by themselves.
a) Second characteristic: sensitivity — the bacteria respond to changes around them (to the oxygen concentration).
b) Concludes that red and blue light are the most effective energy sources for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt_md:
A farmer bought a piece of land on an island. He started planting some young plants far apart in his fruit farm.

**a.** What is the advantage of planting the young plants far apart?

After some time, the farmer noticed that plants from the fruit farm could be found in other parts of the island, as shown below. The plants growing outside the fruit farm are indicated by **x** in the diagram.

**b.** Suggest how the fruits of this plant are adapted to help it reproduce.

rubric.description: a) Explains that spacing avoids overcrowding, reducing competition for sunlight, space, water or nutrients.
b) Describes a fruit adaptation for animal dispersal — sweet/fleshy/brightly coloured with small indigestible seeds — so animals eat it and pass out or discard the seeds elsewhere.

questions.prompt_md:
Animal B lives in a cold environment. The picture below shows how animal B behaves during summer. Although it is warmer in the summer months, the ground remains frozen.

**a.** Explain why animal B spreads itself out on the frozen ground during the summer months.

Animal B walks on ice as it moves from place to place. The underside of its paw is shown below.

**b.** Explain how animal B is adapted to walk on ice.

rubric.description: a) Spreading out increases the surface area of the body in contact with the ice, so the body loses heat faster and the animal cools down.
b) The stiff hair increases friction between paw and ice, so the animal grips better and does not slip.

questions.prompt_md:
The diagram below shows Rachel wearing a heart rate sensor while she is jogging. The sensor detects her heart rate and sends the data to her mobile phone.

Her heart rate during her 30-minute jog is shown in the graph below.

**a.** State the function of the heart in the circulatory system.

**b.** Describe the change in her heart rate and explain why it has to change with time during exercise, as shown in the graph above.

rubric.description: a) States that the heart pumps blood through the blood vessels to all parts of the body.
b) Describes the change: her heart rate increases during exercise.
b) Explains why: the heart must beat faster to transport more blood rich in oxygen and nutrients to the different parts of the body.

questions.prompt_md:
The picture below shows insect P feeding on a stem. This insect inserts its long, pointed mouthpart into the stem to obtain nutrition.

**a.** State the part of the plant stem from which insect P obtains its nutrition.

While obtaining its nutrition, insect P is known to inject a harmful liquid into the stem of the plant. Figure 2 below shows the leaf of the plant turning white after being infested by insect P.

**b.** Based on Figure 2, state which part of the leaf cell was damaged by the liquid to cause the change from green to white.

**c.** Explain how the plant might eventually die if it continues to be infested by insect P.

rubric.description: a) Names the food-carrying tube — the phloem.
b) States that the harmful liquid damaged the chloroplasts in the green leaves, causing them to turn white.
c) Explains that the leaves can no longer trap/absorb light to make food, so the plant starves.

questions.prompt_md:
A point light source is placed 10 cm from a slab of glass. Some part of the glass is covered with a screen except for a gap 20 cm wide.

**Draw the shadow region behind the screen.**

questions.prompt_md:
Consider the electrical circuit below with four identical light bulbs. Initially, no current passes through the ammeter.

**a.** If we want to make the current pass through the ammeter from a to b, should bulb 4 be replaced with another bulb of higher or lower resistance? Explain.

**b.** If bulb 4 is replaced with another bulb of lower resistance, will the total power increase or decrease? Explain.

**c.** If the resistance of bulb 4 decreases, will light bulb 1 become dimmer, brighter, or stay the same brightness? Explain.

rubric.description: a) Answers: lower resistance.
a) Explains that if bulb 4 has lower resistance than bulb 3, more current is needed on that side, so current flows through the ab wire from left to right.
b) Answers: the total power increases.
b) Explains that the total resistance decreases while the voltage stays the same, and P = V²/R, so the power rises.
c) Answers: bulb 1 becomes brighter.
c) Explains that the voltage across bulb 4 (and hence 3) decreases, so the voltage across bulb 1 increases and its power P = V₁²/R₁ rises.

questions.prompt_md:
A dove flies back and forth with a speed of 10 m/s between a port and a ship. The speed of the ship is 2 m/s, moving toward the port. Initially the dove starts from the port, and the distance between the ship and the port is 240 m. Assume the dove never stops to rest.

**a.** When the dove arrives at the ship for the first time, how far is the ship from the port?

**b.** When the dove returns to the port for the first time, how far is the ship from the port?

**c.** What is the total distance travelled by the dove by the time the ship arrives at the port?

rubric.description: a) Finds the time to the first meeting: t₁ = 240 / (10 + 2) = 20 s.
a) Concludes the ship is 240 − 2×20 = 200 m from the port.
b) Recognises the return leg also takes 20 s.
b) Concludes the ship is 200 − 2×20 = 160 m from the port.
c) Total time for the ship: 240/2 = 120 s, so the dove flies 10 × 120 = 1200 m.

questions.solution_md:
**a.** They close the 240 m gap at $10 + 2 = 12$ m/s, so $t_1 = 20$ s and the ship has moved $2 \times 20 = 40$ m: it is **200 m** from the port.

**b.** The dove flies the 200 m back while the ship keeps closing; the return also takes 20 s, leaving the ship $200 - 40 = $ **160 m** from the port.

**c.** The ship needs $240 / 2 = 120$ s to reach the port, and the dove flies the whole time: $10 \times 120 = $ **1200 m**.

questions.prompt_md:
The intensity of the sunlight that reaches the Earth's surface on a certain day is about 1000 W/m². A solar panel with an area of 1 m² is directed so that its surface is perpendicular to the sun's rays. The solar panel output is 25 V and 4 A.

**a.** Calculate the energy dissipated as heat after 1 minute.

**b.** What is the efficiency of the solar panel?

rubric.description: a) Input power 1000 W, output power P = VI = 25 × 4 = 100 W, so the heat is Q = (1000 − 100) × 60 = 54000 J.
b) Efficiency = 100/1000 = 10%.

questions.solution_md:
**a.** $P_\text{in} = 1000$ W and $P_\text{out} = VI = 25 \times 4 = 100$ W, so

$$Q = (P_\text{in} - P_\text{out})\,t = 900 \times 60 = 54000\text{ J}.$$

**b.** Efficiency $= \dfrac{P_\text{out}}{P_\text{in}} = \dfrac{100}{1000} = 10\%$.

questions.prompt_md:
A boy jumps on a trampoline.

**a.** When is the speed of the boy maximum? Is it at maximum height, or when the boy first touches the trampoline, or when the trampoline is at maximum stretch, or somewhere in between? Explain.

**b.** If there is no effort by the boy to jump, the boy will eventually stop bouncing. Where is the energy lost?

rubric.description: a) Answers: somewhere in between first touching the trampoline and maximum stretch.

a) Explains that at first touch the elastic force is still zero so gravity keeps speeding the boy up; only once the trampoline has stretched enough does the elastic force exceed gravity and start slowing him down. The maximum speed is where the two forces balance.
b) States the energy is lost as heat, through friction/air resistance and because the trampoline is not perfectly elastic.
